_comment: App registry. Env vars and secrets are deliberately NOT listed here — gcpdeploy reads the live Cloud Run service and swaps only the image, so this file can never drift out of sync with production.

vacation.unsupported: Retired 2026-09-27 at Erik's request: the Cloud Run service was deleted. Its image is still in Artifact Registry and its database, photo bucket, secrets and vacation-run@ account were kept. Bringing it back is a `gcpdeploy create`, not a ship: see santa-rosa-beach-trip's CLAUDE.md.

beer.note: Ships through the generic pipeline: docker build on the repo's own Dockerfile (which builds the web bundle inside), pushed to the erik-projects registry and patched onto the live service image-only, so the service keeps its env and secrets (the shared anthropic-api-key and cron-secret). The repo's own cloudbuild.yaml / deploy.sh still assume gcloud and are not used from here.

friction._note: Lives in a subdirectory of eriks-projects because the GitHub App cannot create repos. gcpdeploy resolves repo as $REPO_ROOT/<repo>, so this packages the subdirectory alone.

dataviz._note: Subdirectory app, same as friction. Nothing scheduled; verify by opening it.

challenge._note: The test lab: one service at challenge.strongtechnicalconsulting.com hosting every trial app at /<slug>, one database with per-app collection prefixes. First deploy: gcpdeploy create challenge. See challenge/CLAUDE.md.

nextmove._note: Subdirectory app like friction. One image, two entrypoints: the service runs server.js; Cloud Run JOBS nextmove-daily / nextmove-weekly / nextmove-comp run `node jobs/run.js <job>` on the same image. `ship` updates the SERVICE image only - after a ship, PATCH each job's template image to the same digest (see apps/nextmove/CLAUDE.md, 'Shipping a change'). The scheduler targets the jobs:run API, so `verify` starts a job and reads control/last-run, which lags until that run finishes (minutes). Data that grows lives in BigQuery dataset nextmove (us-central1).
